speaker: Doctor
text:
GREETING: I am Dr. Agent. You have presented with double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; to understand the cause, where exactly do you feel the weakness in your arms?

REQUEST TEST: Strength_assessment_upper_limb, Gait_assessment, Eye_movement_analysis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Strength_assessment_upper_limb: Diminished motor strength observed in the upper extremities; Gait_assessment: Not explicitly detailed but consistent with diminished upper limb strength and ptosis affecting upward gaze; Eye_movement_analysis: Presence of ptosis (drooping of the right upper eyelid) that worsens with sustained upward gaze.

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The symptom of worsening weakness with exertion is not typical for Tuberculosis, so we must investigate further. Can you describe the nature of your double vision and tell me if you experience any numbness or tingling in your limbs?

REQUEST TEST: Electromyography (EMG), Nerve_Conduction_Velocity, MRI_Head_and_Neck.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electromyography: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation; Nerve_Conduction_Velocity: Normal; MRI_Head_and_Neck: No abnormalities detected.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.

The EMG results showing decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation (decremental response) combined with your symptoms of weakness worsening with exertion and normal nerve conduction velocities are highly specific for Myasthenia Gravis, confirming the diagnosis despite the lack of findings on MRI.
